sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Administration of Employee Share Incentive Plans (ESOP Trusts)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of France and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (signed 31 May 1984, entered into force 1985)
Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement between France and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2004)
Convention between France and Singapore for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 13 June 2011, in force)
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force 1 February 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code Articles L.561-1 through L.561-60 (AML/CFT customer due diligence and beneficial owner obligations), including Articles L.561-46 to L.561-49 (RBE beneficial owner declaration and register); French Commercial Code Articles L.227-1 et seq. (SAS); EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843 as transposed; implementing French regulations under Articles R.561-1 through R.561-59. For a common-law trust holding shares, the trustee, any protector, and the beneficiaries with a direct or indirect economic interest of at least 25% must be declared as beneficial owners.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (plus statutory access for French and European AML/CFT authorities, financial intelligence units, and regulated AML obligated entities; no general public access after the CJEU ruling of 22 November 2022, Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Biometric passport or other government-issued photographic identity of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport or identity authority of each UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, certificate of incorporation, and directors register of any corporate ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company register or competent corporate registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual tax residence certificate of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the UBO's country of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address for each UBO, such as a utility bill, tax notice, or bank statement issued within the last three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility provider, tax administration, or banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a public authority; otherwise notarization followed by French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation into French of all non-French documents and apostilled originals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator certified by a French appellate court or by a competent French consular officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The certified translation is accompanied by the apostilled original; no separate apostille is required when the translation is issued by a sworn translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, presidents, signatories, trust settlors, trustees, and beneficiaries against (i) the French National Financial Sanctions framework and Tracfin guidance, (ii) the UN Consolidated List, (iii) EU autonomous sanctions lists, (iv) the OFAC SDN list for any USD-clearing or foreign-currency transaction, and (v) national politically exposed person (PEP) registers under French Monetary and Financial Code Articles L.561-10 and R.561-1 et seq. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, PEP family member, PEP close associate, or any beneficial owner holding more than 25% of the SAS. Screening results must be refreshed on each KYC update, on any change of UBO, and immediately upon publication of new sanctions listings.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) with official availability search through INPI's Registre National des Entreprises (data.inpi.fr) and Infogreffe / registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Toubon Law (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994), all statutory documents and mandatory French filings must be in the French language. The SAS legal-form suffix must appear in the dénomination sociale. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Roman characters for registration in the RNE. Foreign-language names are permitted only if they are not misleading and the corporate form remains clear. A proposed name will be refused if it is identical or confusingly similar to a pre-existing INPI trademark, RCS corporate name, or a protected trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Guichet unique, INPI, or the commercial registry rejects the proposed dénomination sociale, the applicant may (i) request an internal administrative review by the relevant Greffe within fifteen calendar days of the rejection notice, (ii) obtain written consent or a coexistence licence from the prior right holder where the refusal is based on an earlier trademark or trade name, or (iii) bring an appeal before the competent tribunal de commerce, or the tribunal judiciaire for intellectual-property grounds, seeking reversal of the refusal. Urgent applications may be made by référé. The refusal must be re-filed through the Guichet unique after correction of the name; no separate registry appeal fee is charged. France does not operate a formal statutory name-reservation system, and the 30-day value reflects the administrative validity period assumed for the preliminary INPI/Infogreffe availability search in the incorporation due-diligence pipeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk administrative ISIC 6430 SAS provided the service provider is a registered domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under Articles L.123-44 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, the contract runs for at least one year, and the address physically receives service of process, mail, and administrative notices. A mere mailbox or non-verifiable co-working reception desk is not sufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<10% probability in the first year) absent tax audit flags; the Greffe and tax or URSSAF authorities retain the right of verification but do not systematically inspect registered offices of service-only SAS structures.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI/Infogreffe name and trademark availability search and official due-diligence extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory online register fee and public register copy tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS statuts (articles of association) by a French avocat and legal opinion on the administration of employee share incentive plans
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SAS formation and corporate legal opinion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization fees for qualified contribution or authentic signature if shareholders elect notarial statuts (optional)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff under the notaires rate schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) submitted in the formation file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI via Guichet unique

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAS incorporation filing fee, fixed taxes, and RNE registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed fee and fiscal stamp duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Kbis extract and official certificate of incorporation for registered-office due diligence
Consular legalization / apostille bundle for UBO passport, corporate good standing, tax residence, and address proof
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / French consulate / competent court or registrar of the origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular and apostille fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of non-French UBO and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing tariff for certified translations in French civil procedure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement for one year (virtual or business-center address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market annual rental for commercial domiciliation in the selected French city

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening database setup and screening refresh covering the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent AML compliance provider / Tracfin-compliant screening software vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for licensed sanction screening and PEP database subscription

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II Title II Chapter VII, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general incorporation rules under Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; RCS registration provisions under Articles L.123-1 to L.123-12 and R.123-1 to R.123-151; Décret n°84-406 of 30 May 1984; mandatory electronic filing through the Guichet Unique pursuant to Article L.123-36.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry), acting as registrar for the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); mandatory electronic filing channel is Le Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) executed by all shareholders, submitted with the online company-creation dossier and, where applicable, the official M0 information set equivalent to Cerfa n°15884*03 (déclaration de constitution de personne morale).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an SAS there is no statutory minimum share capital; the articles freely set capital. Cash contributions are deposited into a blocked account opened in the company's name with a French bank, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until the RCS/Kbis extract is obtained. Unless the articles require full payment at subscription, at least one-half of each cash share's nominal value must be paid up on subscription and the balance may be paid within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the subscriber hereby adopts the Statutes of the company, appoints the President and executive officers named therein, and adopts the registered office at the address stated in the registered-office certificate.

RESOLVED, that all cash subscriptions set forth in the shareholders' register are approved, and that the President is directed to procure the blocking of the funds until the company is entered in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.

RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to publish the legal notice, to sign the declaration of absence of conviction, to file the M0 form and all supporting documents, and to request the Kbis certificate.

RESOLVED, that the corporate books and registers are established at the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and RCS/INPI pre-filing identity check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI online trademark database and Infogreffe RCS company search; no official name-reservation system applies to ordinary commercial companies in France.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a conflict search in RCS and INPI databases; verify the proposed French corporate name, business purpose, domain and trademarks; record the search evidence. If clear, use the selected name in the draft statutes.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and business purpose in French
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No formal objection right exists; if a confusingly similar pre-existing name or trademark appears, select a distinctive secondary element, obtain a coexistence consent letter from the prior right holder, or amend the corporate identity and reconfirm availability.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting French statutes and internal governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and their legal counsel; final text reviewed by the Greffe or notary as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-law SAS statutes containing the legal form, corporate name, object in French corresponding to administration of employee share incentive plans and ESOP trusts, registered office, share capital and subscription table, duration of 99 years, governance powers of the President, share transfer restrictions, and decision-making rules. Where a contribution in kind is made, obtain a commissaire aux apports valuation report if required by law.
required_dossiers: Valuation report for contributions in kind, if any
Registered-office address proof or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory clauses are defective, amend before execution; if the Greffe raises a legal query, correct the clause and, if already registered, file a corrective amendment with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening blocked share-capital account and depositing cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French first-tier bank, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a French notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: In the name of the société en formation, subscribe the cash shares and deposit the agreed paid-in amount into a blocked account. The deposit institution issues an attestation de blocage des fonds listing the shareholders, deposit amounts and release conditions restricted to presentation of the RCS/Kbis certificate.
required_dossiers: Cash transfer instruction or bank reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account due to KYC or beneficial-ownership documentation, provide the completed declaration of beneficial owners and the board resolution; alternatively use a notary escrow or another bank to preserve the filing timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory legal notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the annonce légale to an approved JAL with the company name, legal form SAS, capital, registered office, object, duration, name of legal representatives, and the Greffe where the company will be registered. Obtain the attestation de parution after publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is rejected or contains typographical irregularities, reissue a corrected notice; the attestation de parution is indispensable for RCS filing and must be issued in relation to the final registered-object wording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of final statutes and appointment of corporate officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders by private deed (acte sous seing privé) or notarial deed; French notary when preferred.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all shareholders sign the final statutes; record the acceptance of the President (Président) and, where appointed, any Directeur Général; each legal representative signs the statutory declaration of absence of conviction, absence of personal bankruptcy prohibition and absence of legal incapacity. Verify officer compatibility under Article L.227-5 et seq. of the Code de commerce.
required_dossiers: Acceptance letters of President and officers
Identity and address proofs of shareholders and officers
Signed declarations sur l'honneur (non-condamnation, filiation and nationality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder or officer cannot sign or is disqualified, execute a deed of rectification or replace the officer by unanimous written decision; ensure the final statutory text remains consistent with the published legal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration through the Guichet Unique and issuance of Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Le Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); registration processed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online company-creation application with all corporate data, attach the required documents, pay the statutory greffe fees electronically, and submit the dossier. The Guichet Unique routes the file to the competent Greffe; after verification, the Greffe registers the company, publishes a BODACC notice and delivers the Kbis extract with SIREN/SIRET identifiers.
required_dossiers: Online company-creation form and M0 data set
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Occupancy proof or landlord consent for the registered office
Identity documents and declarations of legal representatives
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Greffe may issue a request for additional documents or a refusal notice; answer within fifteen calendar days with the missing documents. In case of unjustified refusal, file a requête before the president of the Tribunal de Commerce to obtain an injunction, or correct and resubmit the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration formalities and opening of corporate governance books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS/Greffe, INSEE/SIRENE, DGFiP, and the mandatory occupational health service where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon obtaining the Kbis, release the blocked capital with the bank attestation; file the declaration of the beneficial owner (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) with the Greffe within fifteen days; open the share register, minutes book and corporate records; adopt the ongoing governance calendar and register the company with tax and social authorities as necessary.
required_dossiers: Corporate share register and minutes book
Bank attestation authorizing release of blocked funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is late, file immediately to limit penalties; if the Greffe rejects the RBE declaration, correct identity and control details and refile. Any subsequent change of registered office, officers, capital or activity must be filed through the Guichet Unique within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the activity is administrative office administration of an employee share incentive plan/ESOP trust; no industrial installation requires authorization under the French Environmental Code.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for ordinary administration of employee share incentive plans; if the scope expands to discretionary management of financial instruments or third-party assets, an AMF registration or authorization under Articles L.531-1 and L.532-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no classified installation under the ICPE system and no EIA required under Articles L.122-1 to L.122-3 and R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code for an administrative office-only activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges or VOC emissions thresholds apply; office waste must be handled under Articles L.541-1 et seq., municipal sewer/sanitation rules for employee welfare facilities apply, and any electrical or electronic equipment must be managed in accordance with WEEE obligations under Articles L.543-1 et seq.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupancy, obtain the building owner's current fire-safety certificate for the leased office premises; maintain fire extinguishers, evacuation signage and an emergency plan. Employee health and safety monitoring must be arranged with a Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail. No structural-load inspection is required for ordinary administrative office occupancy unless the landlord or local building rules require a technical attestation for the specific building category.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE); official portal: https://www.impots.gouv.fr. Corporate legal and establishment registration is coordinated through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS must complete incorporation and establishment formalities through the INPI Guichet unique. The filing transmits information to the Registre national des entreprises and the competent tax authorities. The entity receives a SIREN number for the legal entity and, where applicable, a SIRET number for each establishment. The French corporate tax account is linked to the SIREN and the entity's tax account with the competent SIE. A VAT-liable entity must request or activate a French VAT identification number from the DGFiP. The French VAT number generally consists of the prefix FR, a two-character control key, and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment that is required to register for French VAT applies to the SIEE, submits constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identification of directors and beneficial owners, evidence of taxable transactions, and—where applicable—an appointment of a French fiscal representative. Entities established in another EU Member State generally do not require a French fiscal representative, subject to the applicable EU VAT rules. VAT registration is not itself proof of French permanent establishment or corporate-tax residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). An eligible SAS may elect temporary partnership-style taxation under the French income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, or IR) for a maximum period of five financial years, subject to statutory conditions including qualifying ownership, active commercial or professional activity, fewer than 50 employees, turnover or balance-sheet limits, and qualifying shareholder participation. The election must generally be notified within the statutory deadline and cannot ordinarily be renewed after the five-year period. There is no general United States-style check-the-box election. France applies specific anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive; these rules can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict relief where a cross-border entity or instrument produces a deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcome. An employee share ownership or incentive-plan administration arrangement does not, by itself, create a tax-transparent classification or a special tax-exempt status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), integrated with the European Union VAT system and customs framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For services, the principal French franchise en base de TVA threshold is EUR 37,500 of annual turnover, with a higher tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 under the applicable rules. For supplies of goods, the principal threshold is EUR 85,000, with a higher tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500. These thresholds generally determine eligibility for the small-business VAT exemption rather than the existence of a taxable transaction. A business may be required to register or file VAT returns before reaching the threshold for intra-Community transactions, imports, exports, reverse-charge transactions, or transactions not eligible for the franchise. A French SAS providing employee share-plan administration services should normally assess the services thresholds and the place-of-supply rules separately.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved private platforms (plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, or PDPs), with the public invoicing portal operated by the Agence pour l'informatique financière de l'État serving as the central data-routing infrastructure. From 1 September 2026, all French businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices; issuance obligations apply from that date to large enterprises and tax groups and from 1 September 2027 to medium-sized, small, and micro-enterprises, subject to the legally applicable implementation timetable. Domestic B2B invoices must use a structured or hybrid format and transmit required invoice data, payment data, and, where applicable, transaction data. France does not generally operate a universal pre-clearance requirement under which every invoice must receive real-time tax-authority approval before issuance. Cross-border B2B invoices, B2C transactions, and transactions outside the domestic mandatory scope may remain subject to electronic reporting or other digital-data requirements. Businesses must maintain audit-ready electronic records and comply with French invoice-content, retention, authenticity, integrity, and accessibility requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT where the exporter is able to prove exportation and the goods have exited the EU customs territory. The principal evidence is an accepted export customs declaration linked to an electronic exit result or equivalent customs proof. Supplies to another EU Member State are generally exempt intra-Community supplies rather than exports and require valid customer VAT identification, transport evidence, and reporting compliance. B2B services are generally taxed at the customer's establishment under the EU place-of-supply rule and are invoiced without French VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism; this is not technically an export zero-rating. Services supplied to customers outside the EU may fall outside French VAT where the place-of-supply rules allocate taxation outside France, subject to the nature of the service and special rules. Employee share-plan administration, financial services, securities transactions, and services connected with financial instruments require transaction-by-transaction analysis because exemptions, intermediary rules, and use-and-enjoyment provisions may apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, description, value, currency, and delivery terms
Electronic export customs declaration and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit result or other legally accepted proof that the goods left the European Union customs territory
Transport evidence, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, carrier certificate, or equivalent logistics record
Packing list and, where relevant, import documentation or delivery confirmation in the destination country
Contract, purchase order, and correspondence establishing the export transaction
Evidence linking the invoice, goods, customs declaration, and transport records
Customer identification and, for intra-Community supplies, valid customer VAT identification number and VIES validation evidence
Bank payment evidence or other commercial settlement evidence where relevant to the audit file
For services treated as outside the scope of French VAT, customer establishment or tax-status evidence, service agreement, deliverables, and records supporting the place of supply

An inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory French VAT export document; French VAT substantiation principally relies on customs exit evidence, transport records, and place-of-supply documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline requiring export proceeds to be brought into France within 180 days. Export proceeds must nevertheless be recorded accurately and supported by ordinary accounting, customs, banking, and anti-money-laundering documentation. If zero-rating or an exemption is unsupported, the DGFiP may reassess the unpaid French VAT, deny or recover an input-VAT refund, charge late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month under the applicable rules, and impose administrative penalties. A 40% penalty may apply for deliberate failure or deliberate misstatement, and an 80% penalty may apply for fraudulent conduct or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions. Failure to issue or retain compliant invoices may trigger additional penalties. Customs violations may result in recovery of duties and taxes, seizure, fines, and other customs sanctions. Serious intentional tax fraud can also create criminal exposure, including imprisonment and substantial fines. A company claiming VAT relief must retain the evidence for the applicable statutory retention period and promptly correct unsupported claims; the tax authority may claw back relief for prior periods within the applicable assessment limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, with prudential and anti-money-laundering supervision by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), foreign-exchange policy coordination by the French Treasury Directorate (Direction générale du Trésor), and customs and trade-control administration by the Directorate General of Customs and Indirect Taxes (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and operates within the European Union single market and the euro area. The euro is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax-reporting, beneficial-ownership, and financial-services restrictions. A French SAS may generally receive foreign capital, pay dividends, make permitted intercompany payments, repay shareholder loans, and remit profits to non-resident shareholders without prior foreign-exchange approval. Dividend distributions require distributable profits, approved financial statements, proper corporate approvals, and compliance with French withholding-tax rules, treaty relief, European Union parent-subsidiary requirements where applicable, and beneficial-owner documentation. Interest, royalties, management fees, and service charges require contractual, transfer-pricing, withholding-tax, and substance support. Banks may delay or refuse transactions where source of funds, economic purpose, ownership, sanctions status, tax residence, or supporting documentation is insufficient. Cash and payment-reporting obligations may apply to cross-border transactions and are separate from currency-convertibility rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general requirement to repatriate or convert export receipts into euros within a prescribed period. Export proceeds may ordinarily remain in foreign-currency accounts or be received through SEPA, correspondent-bank, or other permitted payment rails. The company must retain commercial invoices, contracts, transport and customs evidence, payment records, and records supporting the underlying transaction. Export transactions remain subject to EU and French customs, sanctions, export-control, VAT, statistical, and anti-money-laundering requirements. Banks may impose contractual receipt deadlines, documentary requirements, or internal conversion policies even where no statutory surrender rule applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
Banque Populaire Rives de Paris, part of BPCE Group

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment-account, SEPA collection, payroll, card, and foreign-currency payment functionality, provided the provider is an authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution in the European Economic Area and is permitted to passport services into France. An offshore institution without EU authorisation, passporting, a French branch, or a compliant correspondent arrangement should not be used as the sole treasury bank. An electronic-money account is not a bank deposit and may not provide deposit-guarantee protection equivalent to a credit institution. Fintech onboarding remains subject to French and EU AML, sanctions, beneficial-ownership, tax-residence, source-of-funds, transaction-monitoring, safeguarding, and account-closure controls. A regulated fintech account should supplement, rather than replace, a French or EU credit-institution operating account for capital escrow, statutory payments, payroll continuity, and high-value treasury activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the institution can complete reliable electronic identification, verify the SAS registration and legal representatives, identify and verify all beneficial owners, validate tax-residence and CRS/FATCA information, and assess the business model. Banks may require a physical meeting, notarised or apostilled documents, certified translations, a French address, a local authorised signatory, or an in-person interview for non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, higher-risk countries, unusual payment flows, or unresolved identity and source-of-funds issues. The bank's risk policy controls the practical outcome.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent SAS constitutional records, pending registration, outdated Kbis extract, or mismatch between the bank mandate and registered legal representatives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; articles of association; executed incorporation documents; shareholder and director resolutions; proof of registered office; identity documents for all legal representatives; powers of attorney; up-to-date corporate chart; and confirmation of signing authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unidentified or opaque beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, employee-benefit structures, trusts, or ownership chains involving multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-owner register extract; ownership chart through every intermediate entity to natural persons; shareholder registers; trust or employee-plan documents where applicable; declarations from authorised representatives; identity and address evidence for each beneficial owner; and a written explanation of the ESOP administration model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital injection with unclear source of wealth, source of funds, investment rationale, or remitting party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder resolutions; subscription or contribution agreement; investor corporate records; audited financial statements; bank statements; tax returns or equivalent financial evidence; sale or financing documentation where relevant; remitter-to-investor reconciliation; beneficial-owner evidence; and an investment-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity described as financial, fiduciary, trust, investment, or asset-management activity despite the stated activity being administration of employee share incentive plans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business memorandum; ISIC and French activity classification; service agreements; description of administrative functions; confirmation that the SAS does not accept deposits, provide regulated investment advice, manage third-party assets on a discretionary basis, operate a payment system, or conduct securities dealing; licensing analysis; and sample transaction flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transactions inconsistent with the declared low-risk operating profile, including high-value cross-border payments, rapid pass-through activity, unrelated counterparties, or payments involving high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast; transaction matrix by country, currency, counterparty, and purpose; customer and vendor lists; contracts; invoices; payroll schedules; expected monthly transaction volumes; treasury policy; approval controls; and explanation of exceptional or seasonal flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, politically exposed person, adverse-media, or high-risk-country screening hit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal names, dates and places of birth, nationalities, addresses, tax residences, and ownership data for relevant persons; independent screening results; written false-positive analysis; source-of-wealth evidence; sanctions counsel assessment where required; and enhanced monitoring commitments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to provide CRS, FATCA, tax-identification, or non-resident classification information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French and foreign tax-identification numbers; entity classification analysis; CRS self-certification; FATCA forms where applicable; tax-residence certificates; controlling-person certifications; and supporting corporate-tax records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, uncontrolled virtual accounts, cash-heavy funding, or third-party payments unrelated to the contracting entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury and payment policy; segregation-of-funds procedures; authorised-bank-account list; third-party payment approval protocol; explanation and evidence for any exceptional payment; reconciliation controls; and commitment that operating receipts and capital contributions will be routed through accounts held in the SAS name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-French corporate documents that are unauthenticated, expired, untranslated, or not understandable to the onboarding bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent registry extracts; notarisation or apostille where requested; certified French or English translations; document-validity schedule; officer certificates; and a single indexed electronic data room.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscribed share capital through a French or EEA credit institution into the SAS capital deposit account or, after incorporation, into the SAS operational account designated for equity funding. Use a payment instruction identifying the SAS as beneficiary, the investor as remitter, the legal basis as share subscription, capital increase, shareholder contribution, or shareholder loan, and the precise corporate documentation reference. France generally does not impose a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code regime for ordinary corporate wires; the remitting and receiving banks may nevertheless require a payment purpose, ISO 20022 category purpose, economic-activity code, invoice or agreement reference, and source-of-funds information. Reconcile the remitter, investor, beneficial owner, corporate resolution, subscription agreement, amount, currency, and bank statement. For a capital increase, obtain the deposit certificate and complete the applicable French corporate filings before treating the funds as legally contributed capital. For shareholder loans or intercompany funding, maintain a written agreement, arm's-length terms, transfer-pricing support, withholding-tax analysis, thin-capitalisation and interest-deduction review, and evidence of beneficial ownership. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments where available and SWIFT correspondent transfers for non-euro currencies. Screen all parties, banks, jurisdictions, and payment references against applicable EU and French sanctions requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro supplier and payroll payments, and SWIFT cross-border customer credit transfers for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. Legacy SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers may be supported by correspondent banks, but ISO 20022 cross-border messages, including pacs.008, are the prevailing migration standard. Retain purchase orders, contracts, invoices, delivery evidence, customs records where relevant, tax treatment, beneficiary verification, and payment approval records. For higher-value or jurisdictionally sensitive trade, use a documentary commercial letter of credit subject to UCP 600, with electronic presentation under eUCP where appropriate, or documentary collection subject to URC 522. Establish maker-checker controls, dual approval, beneficiary call-back verification, sanctions screening, duplicate-invoice detection, segregation of duties, and daily bank reconciliation. Do not use payment rails to disguise dividends, shareholder loans, capital distributions, or personal payments as trade disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts with an authorised EU bank or regulated investment firm, supported by documented underlying exposures and board-approved treasury limits.
Non-deliverable forwards where the currency and counterparty market permit them, with documented exposure, valuation, collateral, accounting, and counterparty-credit controls.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for genuine funding or liquidity exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, suitability assessment, collateral terms, valuation controls, and applicable European Market Infrastructure Regulation reporting.
FX spot transactions for operational conversion, including conversion of foreign export receipts or settlement currency into euros, subject to bank AML and transaction-monitoring controls.

Currency options and collars may be used for genuine hedging exposures where the company understands premium, exercise, settlement, liquidity, and accounting risks; speculative trading should be prohibited by treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval and allocation of the financial year's results (décision annuelle des associés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SAS (recorded in the corporate minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after each fiscal year-end, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to adopt within the statutory deadline invalidates the subsequent accounts filing; the President may be ordered by a court to convene the shareholders and may face civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements (comptes annuels) with the Commercial Registry (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month after approval, and in any event no later than seven (7) months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive fine (astreinte) up to EUR 30,000; formal notice may lead to commercial registry strike-off after persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats n°2065 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year companies: file by 15 May; non-calendar fiscal years: within three (3) months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of tax due, late-payment interest of 0.4% per month; extended default may trigger administrative tax reassessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO beneficial-owner statement update (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI via the Guichet Unique (RCS record keeper)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven: within fifteen (15) calendar days after any direct or indirect shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change; no annual re-filing if no change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 for non-disclosure or misleading statement; non-updated record may obstruct subsequent corporate filings and public registration of share transfers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory auditor's report (rapport du commissaire aux comptes), when audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SAS and Greffe (annexed to the annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Report must be completed before the annual shareholders' meeting; filed with the RCS within the seven (7) month accounts-deposit deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of a mandatory audit report invalidates the annual accounts approval; court may appoint an auditor and impose liability on the President.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) must be appointed when the SAS exceeds at least two of the three thresholds: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; turnover excluding taxes > EUR 8,000,000; average staff > 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (ANC règlement n°2014-03 / Plan Comptable Général); IFRS is optional only for consolidated accounts, not for the SAS's individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not require a standalone annual UBO re-filing; the registered beneficial-owner declaration must be updated within 15 days after each share transfer or change in beneficial ownership. The annual shareholders' meeting serves as the annual register verification point; if no change has occurred, no new UBO declaration is filed.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 250 - US$ 800 per year for a commercial registered office in France; full corporate representation and agent services add US$ 1,200 - US$ 4,500 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 4,500 - US$ 18,000 for a statutory audit of a non-listed SAS; ESOP trust administration variants may elevate the range toward US$ 20,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on first EUR 42,500 taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover below EUR 10m); Patent Box 10% on net qualifying intellectual property income; Research Tax Credit (CIR) 30% up to EUR 10m annual research expenditure; Innovation Tax Credit 20% on prototype design costs; employee share ownership incentive deductions; unlimited loss carryforward subject to annual EUR 1m plus 50% excess cap; one-year loss carryback limited to EUR 1m.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065-SD and annexed schedule 2050-2060 (l.iaison fiscale); e-filing through the impots.gouv.fr professional platform (EDI-EFI / FI) or online 'Espace Professionnel' for entities requiring electronic filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year close; for a fiscal year ending 31 December, the electronic filing deadline is 3 May of the following year (extended to 5 May for non-electronic backup or medium enterprises). Non-calendar year-end companies must file by the last day of the third month after their accounting period closes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the SAS, SIREN, French legal form, registered office street address, and principal activity code (APE/NAF).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the SAS is owned by a non-resident, state the French head office and the postal address of the local management; do not enter the foreign parent's address as the French tax address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit or loss for the fiscal year after statutory accounting, before statutory add-backs and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity filing only for a French permanent establishment must report only the French-source profit, after deduction of directly allocable costs and a proper apportionment of head-office overheads.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year loss carryforward applied against the current year's taxable profit, respecting the EUR 1m plus 50%-above-1m annual cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French branch losses may be carried forward only if they relate to French permanent-establishment activity and if all historical filing obligations have been met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation tax credits for research, innovation, patents, or employment structures, primarily the Research Tax Credit and Employee Shareholding Tax Credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers may claim only the credits available and effectively attributable to a French permanent establishment, e.g., R&D credit on qualifying French laboratory/development costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing exposes a monthly 5% surcharge on net tax due (Article 1728 CGI), after the first incident; non-filing after formal notice adds 10% of the final tax. Late interest accrues at 0.20% per month; fraudulent omissions increase penalties to 40%–80%, with criminal consequences of up to EUR 250,000 fines and imprisonment where Article 1741 applies.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on distributions to non-resident corporate beneficiaries (Article 119 bis CGI); 12.8% plus 0.7% solidarity levy for qualifying non-resident individuals; 0% for EU parent companies holding at least 10% shareholding during 24 consecutive months under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive; DTA rates generally 0%, 5%, 10% or 15% according to residence, holding, and effective-beneficial-owner criteria.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its competent tax authority and transmit it to the French paying entity before payment, accompanied by a Form 5000 (Standard Form 1 under O.E. or the prescribed EU dividend certificate). The French entity applies the treaty-reduced withholding rate at source. Where a higher rate was withheld, the non-resident must file a refund application on Form 2570 with the French tax administration (SIE) within the two-year limitation period from the end of the year in which the distribution was made. EU parent-subsidiary warehouse: a 'mother-daughter' statement (Formulaire 5040) and proof of shareholding period must be submitted on request.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding under Article 182 B is 30% for non-resident licensors; DTA and EU Interest & Royalty Directive commonly reduce the rate to 10% (industrial patents) or 0% (pure copyright transfers). Interest: domestic withholding is generally not applied to interest paid to foreign corporations outside controlled tax-havens; where applicable (profit-sharing loans, tax-avoidance schemes), the statutory rate is 30%, mitigated under most treaties to 0%, 5% or 10% depending on the creditor and the underlying debt instrument.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million annual consolidated turnover or total balance-sheet assets triggers the full Local File and Master File obligation (Articles L.13 AA, L.13 AB CGI). Entities with annual cross-border controlled transactions of at least EUR 200,000 must keep a simplified version of transfer-pricing documentation subject to on-demand production.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate jurisdictional 'Economic Substance Regulations' regime for standard trading companies, but applies the full OECD/BEPS substance doctrine through the General Anti-Abuse Rule (abus de droit, L.64 LPF) and treaty-access conditions. The ESOP trust administrator must show real economic presence — physical office, payroll, day-to-day management, independent board, client-file custody, and actual decision-making in France — to avoid treaty denial, thin-capitalisation (Article 212 CGI), and BEPS-destination penalties. French tax charters entitle the tax administration to proportionate re-characterisation when a corporation lacks the capacity to generate its reported income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of tax base, for example inaccurate ESOP accounting, omission of dividend or royalty revenue, fabricated expense deductions, falsifying the profit-and-loss account, filing zero results for several years while distributing profits to foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late payment interest 0.2% per month; deliberate bad-faith penalty of 80% of the asserted tax (Article 1729 CGI). Criminal sanction under Article 1741 CGI: up to 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 250,000 fine (EUR 2,000,000 for a legal person), loss of licences, and public publicity of the decision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution of the evaded tax, face interlacing of debt recovery on personal assets, temporary ban on managing legal persons, travel bans and expulsion orders; when active concealment is shown, the director can be imprisoned under ordinary criminal rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SAS as a 'ghost' vehicle with zero employees, corporate assets, or French management, inserting it into a tax-treaty chain solely to re-route ESOP dividends or to claim treaty exclusive jurisdiction over profit; economic reality does not coincide with legal form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A GAAR recharacterisation neutralises the scheme and the whole tax advantage is repaid (Article L.64 LPF); 100% anti-abuse penalty on the tax avoided if it is proved that the arrangement has no other commercial reality; inadmissibility of the treaty claim and automatic single corporate taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the veil allows the tax administration to recover the tax from directors as guarantors if they have transferred, concealed or dissipated assets. A travel ban (interdiction de sortie du territoire) is issued where the unpaid tax exceeds EUR 5,000; foreign nationals may be prohibited from entry to the Schengen territory and may face criminal confiscation of private assets in lieu of corporate debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money-Laundering / CFT Failure by ESOP Trustee
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Administering an employee share incentive trust without implementing KYC and beneficial-ownership identification covering all participants and ultimate beneficiaries, failing to file a suspicious-transaction report to Tracfin when equity redemption funds are transferred offshore, or intentionally disguising the ultimate beneficial owner of the trust.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Monetary and Financial Code (Articles L.561, L.562? ): individuals are exposed to up to 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine; legal persons face a EUR 2,500,000 fine, asset confiscation, prohibition on conducting financial trust business for up to 3 years, and removal from the French administrator register. The ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) may issue sanctions up to EUR 10m plus 5% of turnover in more serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for any deliberate laundering participation; civil courts may order damages, freezing of personal bank accounts, and professional occupation bans. The prosecutor may impose travel restriction if money flow involves a foreign high-risk state, and directors may be committed for immediate bail where recidivism is shown.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Material failure to prepare and submit the Local File / Master File within the required period (30 days from the tax authority's summons), refusal to provide an annual transfer-pricing summary, or deliberately erroneous benchmark selection for intercompany equity-based compensation or management-fee allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late documentation fines: EUR 10,000 per missing document; a fine equal to 10% of the reassessed amount if the documentation is absent at audit; full adjustment of transfer price, additional 40% penalty for bad faith, and interest accrual. For privileged failure, a penalty of EUR 50,000 may be issued for non-response after notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Documentation failures directly engaged in by the statutory director can trigger personal recovery of the additional deficit, and in egregious circumstances the director's property can be sold and a director ban pronounced. Recklessness in intercompany pricing can be construed as a tortious civil fault, leading to personal monetary compensation to the French tax authority.
